schema_registry.object_rule: Every model-visible object is validated by its registered schema and every schema object has additionalProperties=false. Semantic checks below are applied after schema validation without repair.

content_construction: exact registered prompt-file UTF-8 bytes ending in exactly one LF
RFC8785_JCS allowed-state object followed by LF
RFC8785_JCS registered output-schema object followed by LF
provider_request.chat_template: resolved executable-lock chat template applied exactly once
forbidden_model_visible_metadata: audit event or generated audit annotation

response_parser.accepted_shape: one bare UTF-8 RFC8259 JSON object

namespaces.label: label:<ascii-lowercase-public-slug>
namespaces.anchor: No anchor: namespace exists. Every anchor position is an animal: atom.

reader_query_rule.common: Exact registered arity, exactly one null, and exact namespaces in every non-null position.
reader_query_rule.ROLE_APPLICATION: Only [animal,null,animal-anchor] and [animal,target,null] are legal; [null,target,animal-anchor] is forbidden.

model_local_identity.public_event_aliases: E000000 through E000045 in chronological life-local order; E aliases are audit/projection identities and are never model-citable.
model_local_identity.witnessed_row_aliases: Each Ei deterministically projects before WAKE to Mi, so witnessed rows are M000000 through M000045.
model_local_identity.proposal_ids: For proposal slot s in 0..99, the first schema-valid nonduplicate CREATE receives P(001000+s) formatted as six decimal digits.
model_local_identity.dreamed_row_aliases: A SUPPORTED owner proposal at slot s creates M(001000+s) formatted as six decimal digits; PASS, duplicate, malformed, CONTRADICTED, and UNRESOLVED leave that alias unused.
model_local_identity.copy_on_write: Prefix aliases retain PREFIX origin. OWN and DIST start from the same sealed prefix but independently own any supported return-slot rows. No citation resolves across lives or sibling branches.
model_local_identity.model_visible_identity: Only the local M alias is visible to DREAM or SELF_CHECK; THINK sees only request-local H handles.

proposal.record: Immutable proposal.schema.json audit object {proposal_id,slot,kind,fields,citations,semantic_hash,audit_prediction,audit_confidence,proposal_hash}; it is not a memory row and has no row status, support basis, depth, record hash, or cognitive owner before SELF_CHECK.
proposal.SELF_CHECK_projection: Only {proposal_id,kind,fields,citations} enters self_check_state.schema.json; slot, hashes, prediction, and confidence remain audit-only.
proposal.citation_rule: Exactly 2..8 distinct visible M rows in emitted order, all owned before the proposal slot and all WITNESSED or SUPPORTED.
proposal.ownership: Within one external life and the current branch ancestry (PREFIX plus OWN, or PREFIX plus DIST), the first schema-valid CREATE for a semantic hash reserves the sole proposal owner. A later identical CREATE in that ancestry is a duplicate audit event, creates no proposal owner or row, and its reserved SELF_CHECK opportunity is not dispatched. Sibling-branch and cross-life namespaces never resolve into one another.

self_check_dispatch.count: Exactly one reserved opportunity for each schema-valid new owner proposal; zero for PASS, malformed or illegal CREATE, or duplicate CREATE.
self_check_dispatch.premises: Exact closed cited rows in proposal-citation order.
self_check_dispatch.additional_rows: Zero through eight eligible non-premise rows from the kind-specific pool, sorted by semantic_hash then row_id and truncated to eight.
self_check_dispatch.ROLE_EQUIV_pool: Eligible ANIMAL_VALUE(proposed animal,source,label) and SOURCE_VALUE(proposed anchor,source,label) rows that participate in at least one pair sharing the exact source atom.
self_check_dispatch.CAUSAL_JOIN_pool: Eligible ROUTE(valve,proposed source) and EFFECT(valve,proposed target,effect) rows that participate in at least one pair sharing the exact valve atom.
self_check_dispatch.ROLE_APPLICATION_pool: Eligible SUPPORTED ROLE_EQUIV(proposed animal,proposed anchor) rows and WITNESSED TARGET_BASELINE(proposed anchor,proposed target,mixture) rows.
exclude: rows owned at or after the proposal slot

self_check_reduction.common: premise_ids must byte-equal proposal citations in the same order; support_row_ids must be distinct, drawn only from supplied additional_rows, preserve their relative order in additional_rows, and satisfy len(premise_ids)+len(support_row_ids)<=8. Because additional_rows exclude proposal premises, the canonical accepted-row citation union is premise_ids followed by support_row_ids; first-occurrence deduplication is still applied defensively and must leave the same sequence.
self_check_reduction.SELF_REVIEW_SAME_EVIDENCE: SUPPORTED with an empty support_row_ids array.
self_check_reduction.MODEL_CLAIMED_DISTINCT_LINEAGE_SUPPORT: SUPPORTED with at least one named support row whose public-event lineage is nonempty and disjoint from the union of every premise lineage.
self_check_reduction.harness_judgment: Schema, supplied IDs, order, visibility, lineage nonemptiness, and set disjointness only; never semantic entailment or private truth.
self_check_reduction.SUPPORTED: Create one immutable DREAMED row with the proposal kind and fields, citations equal to the full canonical proposal-premise plus model-identified support-row union, the emitted support basis, status SUPPORTED, depth 1+max(depth over every row in that full citation union), and lineage equal to the set union of every cited row's public-event lineage. No identified supporting premise may be discarded.
self_check_reduction.CONTRADICTED_or_UNRESOLVED: Append an audit receipt and create no cognitive row.
self_check_reduction.malformed_or_illegal: Append an invalid SELF_CHECK audit receipt and create no cognitive row.
self_check_reduction.false_support: A structurally valid false model-supported row remains eligible and may damage later behavior.

hashes.canonical_owner: The earliest schedule owner of one semantic_hash is canonical. Later identical CREATEs never mutate it. Conflicting missing-field values have different semantic hashes, remain separate rows, and cause reader CONFLICT.

DREAM.trigger: Always one M row. WAKE public event Ei is first projected to witnessed Mi; no EVENT object and no E citation ever enters DREAM.
DREAM.rows: Trigger is element zero followed by zero through five selected neighbors; no duplicate row IDs.
DREAM.focus: NO_FOCUS or the one registered CAUSAL_JOIN_FOCUS. It is non-evidentiary and may not be cited.

SELF_CHECK.proposal: Immutable proposal object, never a provisional or mutable row.
SELF_CHECK.premises: Exact proposal-cited M rows in identical order.
SELF_CHECK.additional_rows: Zero through eight rows selected by the fixed public rule.

THINK1.state_tokens: ASCII-byte-sorted unique RECIPE label field values from the sealed typed public projection, sealed before the first heldout provider dispatch, required to byte-equal the later recipient M0 WITNESSED RECIPE projection, and reused byte-identically in every recipient T and L arm after final-goal reveal.

order: project and seal both seed-5 public event lists and E-to-M plans
project and seal the byte-identical public probe
project and seal the byte-identical host-only withheld final goal and state-token vocabulary
derive and seal the public DIST-control manifest from only those sealed public objects
verify every seed-5 frozen vector and cross-twin equality receipt
only then permit the first heldout DREAM, SELF_CHECK, THINK0, or THINK1 provider dispatch
heldout_pre_dispatch_seal.immutability: Later heldout stages consume the sealed hashes and bytes; they may not reconstruct, revise, or replace any projection or control from model output, memory rows, branch results, scores, or private truth.
heldout_pre_dispatch_seal.failure: Any missing byte, dependency/hash mismatch, projection mismatch, DIST mismatch, or cross-twin mismatch is INVALID_PRECONDITION/PUBLIC_PROJECTION_MISMATCH or INVALID_PRECONDITION/DIST_PUBLIC_DERIVATION_MISMATCH before every heldout provider dispatch.

proposal_slots.WAKE: For event index i=0..45, its proposal slot is i + 2*floor(i/4). Project Ei to Mi, then seal and dispatch this WAKE state.
proposal_slots.REACTIVATE: For k=0..10 after WAKE event index 4k+3, dispatch proposal slots 6k+4 and 6k+5, in that order.
proposal_slots.SLEEP: After WAKE event 45 and every associated REACTIVATE, dispatch proposal slots 68..83 in ascending order.
proposal_slots.RETURN: OWN and DIST each dispatch proposal slots 84..99 in ascending order; corresponding slots share the same request seed. M0 dispatches no return proposal slots.

selector_state.citation_graph_degree: At state-selection time, the number of distinct currently eligible rows joined to the candidate by an outgoing or incoming citation edge in the current branch.
selector_state.creation_slot: Witnessed Mi uses event index i. A dreamed M row uses its proposal slot.
selector_state.increment: Increment the selected trigger row exactly once only after the complete DREAM allowed-state object seals and before dispatch. Neighbor appearances never increment. A failed state seal does not increment.
selector_state.prefix_scope: One PREFIX counter map evolves through slots 0..83.
selector_state.fork_scope: M0 is the sealed prefix map. OWN and DIST each copy M0 counters before slot 84 and then evolve independently; neither branch reads the other's counters or results.

UNDER_LINKED.predicate: Every currently eligible row owned before this slot.

RECENT.predicate: Every currently eligible row owned before this slot.

SUPPORTED.predicate: Every row with origin DREAMED and status SUPPORTED owned before this slot.

trigger_pools_and_order.empty_requested_pool: Advance cyclically UNDER_LINKED->RECENT->SUPPORTED->UNDER_LINKED until a nonempty pool is found. If all three are empty, fail pre-dispatch. requested_mode and realized_mode are audit-only.
trigger_pools_and_order.selection: Choose the first row in the realized ordered pool.

context_rows.WAKE: The newly projected witnessed Mi is trigger and element zero. Append at most five prior eligible rows sharing at least one exact typed atom with Mi, ordered by shared-atom count descending, creation_slot descending, semantic_hash ascending, row_id ascending.
context_rows.REACTIVATE_SLEEP_RETURN: The selected trigger is element zero. Append at most five other eligible rows that are citation-adjacent to the trigger in either direction or share at least one exact typed atom. Order by citation-adjacent true first, shared-atom count descending, absolute creation-slot distance ascending, semantic_hash ascending, row_id ascending.
context_rows.typed_atom_equality: Namespace and complete UTF-8 atom bytes must match; equal suffixes in different namespaces do not match.

focus_return_selector.scheduled_side_pool: Eligible rows containing the exact registered source atom for SOURCE_SIDE or exact registered target atom for TARGET_SIDE.
order: number of exact focus atoms present descending
focus_return_selector.fallback: If the scheduled-side pool is empty, use the other-side pool with the same order. If both are empty, realize UNDER_LINKED using its exact pool and order.
focus_return_selector.NO_FOCUS: Use SLEEP_and_NO_FOCUS_RETURN mode at return index slot-84.
focus_return_selector.focus_visibility: Only the prospectively registered focus object enters DREAM state. Selector counters, side, and fallback are audit-only.

return_branches.OWN_focus: If THINK0 terminates REQUEST_RETURN with the exact probe CAUSAL_JOIN, use its source and target. If THINK0 terminates DEFER or any valid system/trace failure, use NO_FOCUS. THINK0 DEFER is trace-local and nonfatal to the stage: OWN and DIST still execute their fixed sixteen slots, but feedback/return credit is impossible and aggregate classification waits until all prospective traces seal.
return_branches.DIST_focus: Always use the sealed prospective DIST control, independent of THINK0 result.

inputs: sealed typed public ROUTE events plus their predetermined M aliases
sealed typed public EFFECT events plus their predetermined M aliases
prospective_DIST_derivation.primary_gap: In the sealed typed public projection, at the public probe target resolve exactly one ROUTE for the public probe source and exactly one EFFECT for that route valve; primary_gap is the absolute difference of their public event indices.
prospective_DIST_derivation.candidate_pool: Every source other than the public probe source having exactly one typed public ROUTE and exactly one typed public EFFECT for that route valve at the public probe target, with absolute event-index gap strictly greater than the frozen context_observation_budget 12, and with the same source/target/predetermined-M aliases in both twins.
prospective_DIST_derivation.selection: Choose the candidate minimizing (absolute(candidate_gap-primary_gap), source atom) lexicographically. Seal {source,target=public probe target,route_row_id,effect_row_id,candidate_gap,primary_gap} plus derivation input hashes before the first heldout model provider dispatch.
prospective_DIST_derivation.twin_rule: Both seed-5 twins must independently reproduce the required vector with unique route and effect resolutions. Missing, multiple, cross-twin-different, or vector-mismatching resolution is INVALID_PRECONDITION/DIST_PUBLIC_DERIVATION_MISMATCH before every heldout model provider dispatch.

matched_fields: sealed prefix rows and counter snapshot
16 return slots and source/target side sequence
DREAM and conditional SELF_CHECK schemas, prompts, generation profiles, and slot seeds
return_branches.independence: OWN and DIST reducers and counters evolve independently after the fork. M1_OWN is fixed for transport regardless of M0, DIST, THINK0, or later score.

SELF_CHECK.meaning: owner proposal slot; dispatched only for a schema-valid nonduplicate CREATE

seed_derivation.pairing: The seed bytes contain no life, latent bit, branch, arm, result, answer, or lock hash. Corresponding twin, OWN/DIST, and matched arm profile+slot pairs therefore share seeds.
seed_derivation.slot_encoding: Unsigned four-byte big-endian integer. Thinker operation ordinal equals slot+1.

previous_read.NO_READ: Initial value and value after THINK or BACKTRACK.
previous_read.NOT_FOUND: One atomic query produced no value; expose only type and request-local read_handle.
previous_read.CONFLICT: One atomic query produced at least two distinct missing-field values; this is a legal read result and exposes only type and request-local read_handle.
previous_read.ROW: Expose only type, request-local read_handle, kind, complete fields, WITNESSED or SUPPORTED status, and semantic_hash.

reader_and_scratch.read_handle: A QUERY at thinker operation ordinal n receives H followed by n as six decimal digits, so operation 1 uses H000001 and operation 12 uses H000012. Handles never cross traces.

scratch.QUERY: Execute one atomic read, allocate its H handle, append a QUERY node containing the exact query and only result type+handle, and expose the full allowed result only as next operation previous_read.
scratch.THINK: Append exact text and already-returned H citations; set next previous_read to NO_READ.
scratch.BACKTRACK: THINK1 only. Append exact text and already-returned H citations; it does not delete or mutate earlier nodes; set next previous_read to NO_READ.
scratch.terminal_location: Trace only; never append a terminal scratch node.
scratch.citation_rule: Only H handles allocated by earlier QUERY operations in the same trace. COMMIT requires at least one. A handle qualifies as structurally used only when it is returned by QUERY, cited in a later retained THINK or BACKTRACK node whose scratch prefix is passed unchanged into every subsequent request through terminal COMMIT, and cited again by COMMIT. A COMMIT-only citation, prose mention, or returned-but-unreasoned handle is decorative and never earns a causal-use claim.
scratch.schema_bound: Every legal sequence of at most eleven registered nodes is at most 6144 RFC8785_JCS bytes under the registered field limits; violation is implementation/runtime drift, not a model outcome.

twelve_operation_reducer.dispatch_order: Slots 0..11 in ascending order until a terminal or failure. Before each dispatch, validate and seal the closed state and record exactly one dispatch receipt for that opportunity.

operations_1_through_11.valid_nonterminal: Execute it, retain it in the trace, append exactly one scratch node, set previous_read as registered, and dispatch the next opportunity.
operations_1_through_11.valid_terminal: Retain it in the trace, append no scratch node, seal the terminal immediately, and do not dispatch later opportunities.

operation_12.valid_terminal: Retain it in the trace, append no scratch node, and seal its registered terminal result.
operation_12.valid_nonterminal: Execute it and retain its operation and any atomic read result in the trace, append no scratch node because no next request exists, and seal VALID_STAGE_FAILURE/BUDGET_EXHAUSTED.

failure_table.COMMIT: Valid trace terminal; stage classification is deferred to the registered offline scorer and may become VALID_STAGE_PASS or VALID_STAGE_FAILURE.
failure_table.REQUEST_RETURN: Valid THINK0 trace terminal; seal the requested focus and continue the registered stage without assigning a stage validity class by this operation alone.
failure_table.DEFER: Trace-local terminal, not an immediate aggregate-stage classification. THINK0 DEFER fixes OWN to NO_FOCUS, preserves the presealed DIST branch, dispatches both return branches, and makes feedback/return credit impossible. THINK1 DEFER marks only that trace unsuccessful. Aggregate validity is assigned only after every prospectively runnable trace seals.
failure_table.missing_required_abstraction: VALID_STAGE_FAILURE/MISSING_REQUIRED_ABSTRACTION after a root-absence manifest seals; no T traces dispatch.
failure_table.sham_infeasible: VALID_STAGE_FAILURE/SHAM_NOT_IDENTIFIABLE; only T-SHAM is non-dispatched, every other prospectively runnable T arm still executes, and full causal pass is impossible.
failure_table.fidelity_gate_failed: VALID_STAGE_FAILURE/FIDELITY_GATE_FAILED after both registered fidelity sets seal; no L thinker trace dispatches.

opportunity_ledger.exactly_one_record_per_registered_opport: A dispatched opportunity has one provider dispatch receipt. Every registered opportunity not dispatched has one non-dispatch row. No opportunity has both or neither.
opportunity_ledger.post_terminal: Every opportunity after the first terminal or failure receives a non-dispatch row with the closed prior-terminal reason, attempts=0, input_tokens=0, output_tokens=0, and provider_request_id=null.
opportunity_ledger.self_check_reserved: Only a schema-valid CREATE registers a SELF_CHECK opportunity. A new owner dispatches it; a duplicate records NON_DISPATCH_DUPLICATE/DUPLICATE_PROPOSAL. PASS and malformed or illegal DREAM output register no SELF_CHECK opportunity.

semantic_vectors: all nine exact kind/field shapes and every legal one-null query
E-to-M WAKE projection and M-only proposal citations
raw v03r public/probe/withheld-goal/state-token projection and pre-heldout seal ordering
proposal-not-row SELF_CHECK, full premise-plus-support citation union, and all four reduction outcomes
selector pools, counter increments, fork copy, and deterministic ties
seed bytes for every profile boundary slot and paired life/branch equality
operations 1, 11, and 12 for every terminal and nonterminal class
all non-dispatch reasons including missing abstraction, sham infeasibility, and fidelity failure with zero attempts and tokens
pre_dev_golden_vectors.seal_rule: Vectors are generated from the resolved executable lock after human ratification during CPU work, independently reviewed, and sealed before the first DEV dispatch. They verify these proposal bytes and may not choose new semantics.
